scope: Negative privacy and observable-call proof for a proposed parse-only own-property read cache. The candidate exists only as an in-memory transformation and is never enabled in a battle runner.

results.name: JSON.parse replaced before installation leaks the fresh raw root
isProxy callback receives the fresh raw root
WeakMap.prototype.set replaced after installation receives raw keys
Reflect.get replaced after the first read must still run for own properties
wrap(raw) remains uncached and observes host aliases
inherited getters and missing values remain dynamic
canonical children descriptors symbols and write-failure stickiness remain equal on this fixture

conclusions: Capturing JSON.parse during installation does not prove it is the pristine native parser or that raw roots never escape.
Even a pristine parser can leak raw roots through options.isProxy or replaceable raw-receiving WeakMap methods.
Caching skips post-install Reflect.get replacements and their observable effects; capturing an intrinsic changes that existing boundary behavior unless excluded by a proven domain.
Active source and emitted battle loaders call wrap(raw), not membrane.parse, so a parse-only cache does not accelerate the current workload.

No performance benchmark is reported for a candidate rejected by these correctness checks. A future optimization requires a source-backed private-loader boundary and explicit pristine-intrinsic capabilities; host attestation is not inferred.
